evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: the opening paragraph names a free iPhone app for parents of picky kids, explains planning seven dinners from the fridge/cupboard and only buying the gap. The CTA says 'Join the iPhone waitlist' and its adjacent text explains the email outcome.
evidence.fit: The delivered file loads offline at all three required widths; every visible primary/repeated waitlist action requested https://pantrywise.example/waitlist. All 12 shelf choices and three child vetoes work, demonstrating both existing groceries and picky eating; free use and later shared-list pricing uncertainty are disclosed alongside the first CTA.

evidence.honesty: The first-screen CTA explains that one email address joins a waitlist and that the app is not ready; the adjacent family-plan note says its price is unset. evidence.interaction: Mouse/touch/keyboard checkboxes and reset work: empty shelf gives 'Nothing on the shelf'; eggs alone gives three dinners and an explicit short-week explanation; Put the sample back restores nine ingredients and clears all vetoes. Empty, 300-character, zero, negative and multiline pasted text cannot alter boolean controls. Tab focus is visible throughout, Space toggles, Enter opens the menu/FAQ, Escape restores menu focus, and all four FAQ summaries expand/collapse. No page errors. Shopping square marks are decorative, not tickable controls.
evidence.copy: The short-week message explicitly says 'Only 3 dinners fit' in the one-ingredient test, and the empty state does not invent a week. 'Put the sample back' accurately describes reset. Labels such as USES/BUY/KIDS are consistent, though they render at 11px; the opening copy also awkwardly calls seven dinners 'seven weeknight dinners'.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: named audience, concrete seven-dinner promise, waitlist disclosure and the first sample meals coexist within 900px. 390: the CTA and labelled sample shelf begin within 844px, but no planned meal is yet visible. Under reduced motion all required content remained visible; the result-row flash is shortened to 180ms rather than entirely removed.

problems: At 390, bring the meal summary/output closer to the ingredient controls; changing the upper shelf currently updates a plan below the long stacked shelf and veto panel.
Increase the 11px uppercase USES/BUY/KIDS/example micro-labels flagged by the smallest-text probe, especially in the dense phone meal rows.
The shopping list's square marks look like checkboxes but do not accept taps or keyboard focus; either implement tick-off behavior or make their static role clearer.

reason: B has native labelled controls, a working sample reset, meaningful picky-eater states, larger mobile targets and cleaner accessibility probe results. Both load offline and send waitlist actions to the correct destination, but B needs less remedial accessibility and state-management work; a compact phone feedback layout and larger micro-labels would strengthen it further.
